newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem leaves on Pacific Rim tour.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem leaves on Pacific Rim tour.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem left Friday on a tour of Vietnam, Thailand and Singapore to drum up bilateral trade.
Menem, flanked by 50 Argentine businessmen, arrives Sunday night in Vietnam and will hold meetings with Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet Monday and take part in business seminars.
Vietnam's GDP is $21.5 billion and its trade with Argentina totals $10 million, with Argentina enjoying a $5.0 million surplus.

"Argentina's interest in this country resides in the broader context of foreign policy aimed at boosting relations with the Asia-Pacific region, and (we are) studying it as an excellent potential market for us," a Foreign Ministry document said.
Vietnam, which opened up an embassy in Buenos Aires two years ago, has expressed an interest in boosting ties with Latin America and using Argentina as its base of operations.
On Tuesday Menem leaves for Thailand where he will meet King Bhumibol Adulyadej.
Argentine trade with Thailand, whose GDP totals $157 billion and total foreign trade totals $90 billion, ran at $176 million in 1995. Argentina had a $72.5 million surplus.
Thailand, which once slapped stiff restrictions on Argentine beef due to foot-and-mouth disease, currently has 23 Argentine meat-packing plants.
On Thursday and Friday Menem will visit Singapore and take part in seminars on the Mercosur customs union, which is made up of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay.
Singapore's bilateral trade with Argentina runs at $300 million and the trade balance traditionally favors Singapore.
Argentina mainly sells Singapore soyoil and linseed oil.
